newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker despite stock drop due.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker despite stock drop due.

text.p: COMEX copper settled weaker in a market that continues to be gripped by LME stock reports in the absence of fresh fundamental news, traders said.
LME stocks have fallen nearly 130,000 tonnes in the past two months, and another drawn down was expected on Tuesday, with some brokers forecasting a dip of 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes.
Bette Raptopoulos said there was some profit-taking after Friday's surge, and traders were also leery of a resurgence in talk about how much stocks of copper the Chinese held.
"Generally the market remains choppy," Raptopoulos said.
The market shrugged off news that unions and management at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino mine in New Mexico failed again to agree on a new pay deal in talks late last week
Labor talks at the 170,000 tonnes per year contained copper mine are set to continue November 7 though 9. Chino workers have been without a contract since June 30.
December COMEX settled 1.70 cents lower at 95.45 cents per pound, traded 97.30 to 94.80 cents. Spot October went out 1.20 cents weaker at 100.00 cents.
LME three months was barely above the key psychological level of $2,000 per tonne in late London evening trading.
